articles.title: GLP-1 drugs linked to reduced alcohol use and healthier eating in real-world study
articles.summary: Tracking 135 patients across Spain for nearly a year, researchers found that routine treatment with drugs like semaglutide and dulaglutide coincided with lower self-reported alcohol intake and better dietary adherence.

articles.title: Heavy cannabis use linked to mild psychotic symptoms and depressive thoughts
articles.summary: Frequent cannabis use is closely linked to higher rates of mild hallucinations, paranoia, and depressive symptoms, particularly among individuals who begin using the drug heavily at a young age.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
articles.summary: Blockbuster weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may do more than help people shed pounds, with growing evidence suggesting they could also influence brain health. Although studies have linked GLP-1 medications to a lower risk of dementia, major trials found that semaglutide did not slow Alzheimer's disease. Scientists suspect these drugs may be more effective at preserving memory and thinking abilities in people with obesity or diabetes, especially before cognitive problems appear.

articles.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

articles.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
articles.summary: Scientists discovered that although people with and without autism show surprisingly similar average brain activity, individuals with autism exhibit much greater differences from one another, especially in regions involved in social understanding. The findings suggest that traditional research methods may be overlooking crucial differences that could help unlock more personalized autism support.

articles.title: Does personality predict family size? A 15,000-person study across three countries weighs in
articles.summary: A survey of 15,120 adults in Canada, the United States, and Japan suggests that outgoing, cooperative, and emotionally stable people tend to have slightly more biological children, though marriage, age, and national culture play much larger roles.

articles.title: Scientists finally pin down what a mysterious Alzheimer’s gene does
articles.summary: CASS4 has been tied to Alzheimer’s risk since 2013, but nobody knew what it did in the brain. New mouse research suggests it lets immune cells physically grip and compact amyloid plaques.

articles.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene

articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. articles.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements.
